newsitem.title: USA: Mass. Gov. signs $18.4 bln fiscal 1998 budget.
newsitem.headline: Mass. Gov. signs $18.4 bln fiscal 1998 budget.

text.p: Massachusetts Gov. William Weld signed Thursday an $18.4 billion budget for fiscal year 1998, the eighth consecutive year the state's budget has been balanced without new taxes or deficit borrowing.
The budget increases spending over anticipated fiscal year 1997 spending by 3.8 percent and cuts taxes by $54 million.
"This budget is balanced, provides modest tax cuts, and continues out commitment to education reform and to the Commonwealth's cities and towns," Weld said in a statement.

The tax cuts include a 10 percent earned income tax credit for low-income residents, an increase in the dependent child care deduction for families with children under 12 to $1200 from $600, and a tax credit for homeowners of up to $6,000 for septic or cesspool repair.
Gov. Weld also filed legislation to hold back $24 million of the $860 million earmarked for higher education in fiscal 1998, pending a reduction in student fees.
"For the second consecutive year, this budget provides a generous increase for higher education but offers little or no break for students," Weld said.
The budget supports other education initiatives including full funding for kindergarten through grade 12 education reform, Weld said.

To strengthen the state's criminal justice system, the budget included a $36 million increase for the state's court system, including 200 new probation officers, $5 million increase for state police cruisers and a rise of $5 million for community policing.
The spending package also earmarks $107 million in fiscal 1998 funds that, along with $28 million in fiscal year 1997 surplus money, will fully pay off the so-called 1990 Recovery Bonds.
"Wiping out this debt is not purely symbolic -- it is proof positive that our fiscal recovery is 100 percent complete," Lieutenant Governor Paul Cellucci said in a statement.
